title: Echo Tap: sandboxed, credit-gated shadowing for low-cost production validation
creator: Diego Morales
description: Introduce an "echo tap" pipeline: a sandbox-first shadowing flow that duplicates a controlled subset of production requests to candidate model backends while enforcing per-tenant credit gates, progressive sampling, and strict isolation so we can validate model behavior without uncontrolled cost or privacy exposure.
acceptance_criteria: Echo Tap can duplicate a request stream with <=0.5ms median added latency on the gateway path when sampling is disabled (measureable in perf CI)
Per-tenant credit buckets exist and prevent any tenant from exceeding monthly mirror budget; mirror attempts beyond budget are dropped and audited
Sampling policy supports stratified sampling (by tenant, request size, and cold-start flag) and can be updated via the Console without code deploy
Mirrored requests are clearly tagged (X-Redwood-Echo:1) and routed to sandbox runtime clusters with zero-write side-effects by default
Console dashboard surfaces per-model, per-tenant mirrored token cost and p95 latency for both original and mirrored paths
Automatic fallback: if mirrored path exceeds cost or error thresholds, sampling is throttled down and owners are notified via PagerDuty alert rule
design_notes: Pipeline model: gateway -> tapizer -> sampler -> credit-gate -> sandbox-proxy -> sink (logs/trace/metrics)

Credit gating: soft notify at 70% of budget, hard stop at 100%; budgets configurable per-tenant via billing API. Budget records are enforced by a distributed lease in the budget service to avoid races.

Isolation: sandbox clusters run in separate VPCs with egress disabled; mirrored requests get a read-only policy and are blocked from writing to external systems. Any integration calls in mirrored flows must be stubbed or routed to replay-only fakes.

Sampling strategy: stratified reservoir sampling with priority boosting for low-frequency tenants and long requests (so regression signals for expensive cases are captured). Rate adapters will lower sample % when global mirror spend approaches budget caps.

Cost accounting: tokens emitted by mirrored requests are counted to a mirror cost ledger and billed to a shadow-chargeback account; per-token cost uses same model-performance profile as serving runtime to estimate spend before hitting budget.

Rollback & safety: automated rollback triggers include mirrored error-rate delta > 2x baseline, mirrored p95 latency > 200ms over baseline, or daily mirror spend > configured percent of committed budget. When triggered: reduce sampling to 0.1% and create an incident ticket with pre-populated diagnostics.
Headers & trace: add X-Redwood-Echo-Version and X-Redwood-Echo-Stage to mirrored requests; tie traces to original request via Redwood-Orig-Trace ID to correlate production vs mirror behavior.
Compatibility: provide a shim to convert streaming responses to non-streaming for models that differ in response mode so side-by-side comparison is feasible in analytics layer.
Data retention: mirrored request bodies are redacted for PII via the mirror-redactor component; retention defaults to 14 days for mirrored payloads and 90 days for aggregated metrics.
Operational UX: Console exposes a "Tap sandbox" modal to create quick experiments scoped to a tenant list with one-click budget and sampling presets (internal, canary, broad-sample).
progress_updates: 2026-02-12: Spike complete — prototype tapizer implemented as a lightweight NGINX Lua filter + sidecar sampler. Perf microbench shows +0.4ms median. (notes: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/echo-tap-spike)

2026-02-18: Design review with Security and Billing. Security requested explicit egress blocks and mandatory redaction pass. Billing requested per-tenant budget API; opened ENG-251102 to implement budget API.
2026-02-25: Implemented per-tenant budget lease in budget-service; integration tests added. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/6123

2026-03-03: End-to-end flow wired to sandbox clusters. First internal canary (team-infra) enabled at 0.5% global sample. Observability: dashboard stub created at https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/echo-tap

2026-03-08: Safety tuning: added exponential backoff to sampling adapters to smoothly reduce load when mirrored path latency rises. Performance regression triggered a follow-up ENG-251450 to optimize KV cache ordering.
2026-03-10: Preparing release branch for runtime-1.32; scheduled canary rollout to 5 internal tenants on 2026-03-15. Security review in progress (ticket SEC-4331).
